title: Shalya: Duryodhana in the lake, the mace fight
hook: the last Kaurava king walks into a lake, and some hunters overhear
tomorrow: Shalya: Duryodhana in the lake, the mace fight

segments.voice: Yesterday, Shalya fell to Yudhishthira's dart, and Sahadeva kept his vow against Shakuni. What did you face steadily, without anger? Day eight hundred forty-five.

One man walks away from the battlefield on foot, carrying a mace. His horse is dead. His army is gone. His brothers, his friends, his commanders have fallen. He is the king the whole war was fought for, and he is alone. On the way he meets Sanjaya, his father's companion, and gives him a message for the blind old king at home: tell my father I've gone into the lake. Then Duryodhana walks down to the water's edge, and keeps walking. Today, a king under the water, and the people who find him.
screen: `ALONE, ON FOOT.` → `TELL MY FATHER.` → `INTO THE LAKE.`

segments.voice: In Ganguli's English, Duryodhana enters the lake and, by a power of illusion he knows, binds the waters around him, so that he can rest beneath them, hidden. It's an eerie picture: the lake smooth and still, and the last Kaurava king lying under it. Three survivors of his army find the lake: Kripa, Ashvatthama and Kritavarma. They stand on the bank and call down to him. Come out, they say. Fight with us. And from under the water he answers: not tonight. I'm wounded and tired. Tomorrow. Then the epic brings in some passersby: hunters, men who bring meat to Bhima's kitchen. They hear the whole conversation, a king speaking from under a lake. And they think: the Pandavas are searching everywhere for Duryodhana. Bhima will reward us. So they go and tell him. The war's last hiding place is given away by a few hunters with a delivery to make. The Pandavas come to the lake with Krishna, and their army fills the shore with noise. And Yudhishthira stands at the edge of the still water and speaks to his cousin underneath it. Why are you hiding, he asks. Come out and fight. Duryodhana answers from below: I'm not afraid. I'm only resting.
screen: `HE BINDS THE WATERS` · `THREE SURVIVORS CALL DOWN` · `THE HUNTERS OVERHEAR` · then, large: `WHY ARE YOU HIDING?`

segments.voice: Sit, and let your body grow still, the way a lake grows still when the wind drops. Breathe in slowly. Breathe out. Notice whether some part of you has been hiding lately, under busyness, under the surface, wanting not to be found. Don't drag it out. Just notice it's there. Breathe in, and let the surface settle. Breathe out, and let what's underneath rest too. If you pray, you can bring it quietly into your prayer. The bell holds the time.
Shalya. The book of the war's last day: the commander fallen, and Duryodhana lying hidden under a lake until hunters give him away.
Your line: not afraid, only resting. Today, notice one thing you're hiding under the surface, and name it to yourself. Day eight hundred forty-five.

howItsDone: Duryodhana's hiding in the lake, told in the Shalya Parva, is retold in readings, regional theater and serials of the Mahabharata, and the lake scene leads into the war's final duel.

pairs: carries word to the blind king

myth: Duryodhana fled the field on horseback with his guard
his horse was dead, his army gone; he walked away alone with his mace.
some hunters who brought meat to Bhima gave away the hiding place
they overheard the king talking from under the water.
Duryodhana told Yudhishthira he was hiding out of fear
he said he wasn't afraid, only resting.

fork.setup: you're one of the hunters. you've just heard a voice from under a lake, and you know the Pandavas are searching for Duryodhana. what do you do?
options: keep walking; it's not your war.
call down to the king and warn him.
fork.reveal: the hunters go and tell Bhima, hoping for a reward, and the Pandavas come to the lake.

original.note: Duryodhana: the eldest Kaurava, hidden under the lake.

trapdoor: what you thought: Duryodhana ran away and hid out of cowardice.
what it means: he says he's wounded and tired, and means to rest before fighting again.
what a scholar hears: the epic lets the hiding place be given away by passing hunters, so the war's end turns on ordinary people overhearing a king.

notes: Editor pass: replaced the narrator's verdict 'small and perfect' with a plain transition.
All paraphrase. Confirm in Ganguli Duryodhana's message to Sanjaya and his binding (Ganguli: 'stupefying') of the waters by illusion.
Confirm that the three survivors are Kripa, Ashvatthama and Kritavarma, and that Duryodhana asks to rest until the next day.
Confirm that the hunters supplied meat to Bhima and told him in hope of reward.
The lake is named Dvaipayana in the text; the script leaves the name out.
Duryodhana's reply ('not afraid, only resting') is paraphrased; tomorrow's script (day 846) continues the conversation.
Audit: fixed a garbled doubled line ('passersby. Hunters happen to be passing by').
